scenarioStory.history: Patient was raking leaves in his front yard approximately 30 minutes ago when he developed sudden, crushing substernal chest pressure, 8/10, radiating to his jaw and left arm. He came inside, sat down, and told his wife he felt 'sick and sweaty.' Denies shortness of breath at rest but reports feeling winded. Associated nausea, denies vomiting. Denies similar pain today prior to onset; reports one prior heart attack five years ago treated with a stent.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 66-year-old male with known prior MI and cardiac risk factors, seated and diaphoretic, reporting classic crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the jaw and left arm that began while raking leaves 30 minutes ago. → 12-lead acquired; ASA and IV started: Crew acquires a 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes, identifies an inferior STEMI pattern, administers chewable aspirin, establishes IV access, and screens for nitrate contraindications before considering nitroglycerin. → NTG given after screening, IV started: After confirming no PDE5 inhibitor use and adequate blood pressure, the crew administers sublingual nitroglycerin and closely monitors hemodynamic status given the inferior (possible RV) involvement. → Prepared for transport with STEMI notification: Patient is packaged and transported to a PCI-capable facility with serial 12-lead EKGs, ongoing reassessment, and early notification of any clinical changes.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Crushing substernal chest pain radiating to jaw and left arm, with diaphoresis

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 66-year-old male with known prior MI and cardiac risk factors, seated and diaphoretic, reporting classic crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the jaw and left arm that began while raking leaves 30 minutes ago.

scenarioEvents.name: 12-lead acquired; ASA and IV started
scenarioEvents.description: Crew acquires a 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes, identifies an inferior STEMI pattern, administers chewable aspirin, establishes IV access, and screens for nitrate contraindications before considering nitroglycerin.
relatedChecklist: Acquire 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes; recognize inferior STEMI pattern
Administer aspirin 324 mg PO, chewable non-enteric-coated
Screen for PDE5 inhibitor use and confirm SBP >100 mmHg before nitroglycerin
Provide advance STEMI notification to the receiving hospital

scenarioEvents.name: NTG given after screening, IV started
scenarioEvents.description: After confirming no PDE5 inhibitor use and adequate blood pressure, the crew administers sublingual nitroglycerin and closely monitors hemodynamic status given the inferior (possible RV) involvement.
relatedChecklist: Nitroglycerin 0.4 mg SL; may repeat q3-5 min if SBP remains >100 mmHg
Continually monitor hemodynamic status given inferior/possible RV infarct; be ready to resuscitate if hypotension occurs

scenarioEvents.name: Prepared for transport with STEMI notification
scenarioEvents.description: Patient is packaged and transported to a PCI-capable facility with serial 12-lead EKGs, ongoing reassessment, and early notification of any clinical changes.
relatedChecklist: Perform serial 12-lead EKGs en route; reassess for clinical change
Transport promptly to appropriate PCI-capable facility, minimizing scene time
Provide early notification to receiving facility of any changes in condition or serial EKGs

scenarioEvents.name: NTG given without PDE5 screen
scenarioEvents.description: The crew administers nitroglycerin without asking about recent PDE5 inhibitor use. The patient, who took sildenafil the night before, develops profound, refractory hypotension.
relatedChecklist: Recognize missed PDE5 inhibitor use as the cause of nitrate-induced hypotension
Hold further nitroglycerin; treat hypotension with IV fluid bolus, prepared to add a pressor

scenarioEvents.name: STEMI recognition delayed
scenarioEvents.description: The crew delays 12-lead EKG acquisition and aspirin administration despite the classic presentation. The infarct progresses untreated and the patient develops worsening pain with early hemodynamic compromise.
relatedChecklist: Recognize delayed STEMI identification; acquire 12-lead EKG immediately
Administer aspirin 324 mg PO chewable now that ACS is recognized

scenarioEvents.name: Symptomatic bradycardia develops untreated
scenarioEvents.description: Vagally-mediated bradycardia from the inferior/RCA-territory STEMI worsens and becomes symptomatic, with hypotension and dizziness, because the crew did not recognize or treat it per the Bradycardia Guideline.
relatedChecklist: Recognize symptomatic bradycardia complicating inferior STEMI (HR 36, hypotensive, dizzy)
Atropine 1 mg IV; may repeat q3-5 min (maximum total dose 3 mg)
